name: LATAM Airlines Group S.A.
moat_justification: Airlines are structurally close to moat-less: the product is commodity, switching costs are minimal and the industry destroyed capital through the last cycle — LATAM itself went through Chapter 11 in 2020 and printed negative owner's earnings in FY2021-FY2022. The roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json is 3.3% / 6.4% / 8.0% / 4.0% for 2016-2019, -39.4% / -93.7% for 2020-2021, then 21.5% / 18.6% / 25.7% / 29.0% for 2022-2025 — the recent strength is real but sits on a bankruptcy-written-down capital base (equity $31M in FY2022 rebuilding to $1,337M in FY2025), so it is not evidence of a through-cycle moat at 7+. What LATAM does have is regional dominance: the largest South American network and hubs, leading domestic positions in its home markets, LATAM Pass, the Delta JV, cargo leadership, and a post-restructuring cost base with gross margin expanding from 24.3% (FY2023) to 29.2% (FY2025). That is a weak-to-moderate franchise in a bad industry: moat 4/10, CAP 7.2 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.7x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier B (17.3%) vs bull-case tier S (27.6%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Largest South American airline, moat 4/10 (regional dominance, structurally weak industry) — clears 15% on post-restructuring numbers (22.4% weighted IRR, IV@15% $80.10 vs $47.47) but the base is a cyclical high and the bear case is Tier B at 17.3%; it does not clear 25% (25% hurdle price $41.27, below the price) — size it like a B.
alert_suppressed_reason: engine output predates release 5.5.0 — re-run the engine before an entry alert; tier exists only because of a judgment override
moat_for: Dominant South American network: hubs at Santiago, Lima and Sao Paulo/Guarulhos and leading positions in the Chilean, Peruvian, Colombian, Ecuadorian and Brazilian domestic markets
LATAM Pass loyalty program plus the antitrust-immunized Delta joint venture feeding North America traffic
Cargo leadership in South America (about 30% regional share, per company/industry reporting) on the same network
Post-Chapter 11 cost and fleet reset showing up in the filings: gross margin 24.3% (FY2023) to 25.5% (FY2024) to 29.2% (FY2025) in fundamentals.json
moat_against: Commodity, price-shopped product with low passenger switching costs; loyalty is the only lock-in and rivals match it

Through-cycle returns are poor: roic_proxy -39.4% (2020) and -93.7% (2021) and only 3.3-8.0% in 2016-2019 — the 18.6-29.0% of 2023-2025 sits on a post-bankruptcy written-down capital base (equity was $31M-$1,337M over 2022-2025)
Cyclicality is proven, not theoretical: Chapter 11 in 2020, owner's earnings negative in FY2021 and FY2022 (OE positive only 3 of the last 5 years)
Fuel and FX: costs are largely USD while a large share of revenue is in BRL and other local currencies; 2026 guidance was cut then reinstated around a fuel shock
Rivals are resetting their own cost bases in Chapter 11 (GOL and Azul in 2025), eroding LATAM's post-restructuring cost edge; Brazilian tax/contingency overhang (Note 30)
